'''Frool''' was a [[Ferengi]] [[waiter]] at [[Quark's]] in [[2372]]. Despite his reluctance to go against ten thousand years of Ferengi tradition, Frool joined [[Rom]]'s [[Guild of Restaurant and Casino Employees]] to protest [[Quark]]'s unfair labor practices.

However, when the [[labor union]] was confronted by [[Brunt]] (an [[Ferengi Commerce Authority|FCA]] [[liquidator]]), Frool immediately caved in before Brunt could say another word, and begged for forgiveness. Frool remained cowering on the floor, desperately hoping for the FCA's mercy. ({{DS9|Bar Association}})

{{bginfo|Frool was played by actor [[Emilio Borelli]].|According to the script, Frool was an older Ferengi and senior waiter at Quark's. The script had this to say about him, "''Frool's seen the best of times and the worst
of times, but has never quite grasped the [[latinum]] ring.''" Additionally, his name was pronounced as "FROOL" (rhymes w/ drool). ''{{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/488.txt}}''|Frool has appeared in several DS9 novels set after {{e|What You Leave Behind}} as well as the ''[[Star Trek: Terok Nor]]'' novel ''[[Dawn of the Eagles]]''.}}

[[Rom]] (cousin) |actor = [[David Jeffries]] (uncredited) }} '''Stol''' was a [[Ferengi]] {{dis|collector|occupation}} and [[cousin]] of [[Quark]] and [[Rom]] who lived during the mid-[[24th century]]. In [[2369]], Stol attended an [[auction]] in [[Quark's]] and bought a [[gemstone|bejeweled]] [[dagger]] that [[Vash]] brought back from the [[Gamma Quadrant]] for 105 {{dis|bar|latinum}}s of [[gold-pressed latinum]]. ({{DS9|Q-Less}}) In [[2371]], [[Ishka]] told Quark that she was writing a [[letter]] to Stol, when in fact, she was conducting business transactions – an illegal activity for a Ferengi [[female]] at that time. ({{DS9|Family Business}}) {{bginfo|According to the call sheet, Stol was played by background actor [[David Jeffries]] in "Q-Less".|For "Q-Less", the call listed him simply as "Ferengi". He filmed his scenes for this episode on Monday {{d|16|November|1992}} on [[Paramount Stage 17]].|Stol is mentioned in ''[[Legends of the Ferengi]]'' by [[Ira Steven Behr]] and [[Robert Hewitt Wolfe]]. Quark sends Stol a bejewelled [[Klingon]] dagger, five [[Bajoran]] earrings, a [[combadge]], a [[tricorder]] and a gross of [[self-sealing stembolt]]s.}} == External link == * {{mbeta}} [[de:Stol]] [[Category:Ferengi]] [[Category:Quark's family]]

'''Qol''' was a [[male]] [[Ferengi]] who claimed to be a member of the [[Ferengi Trade Mission]] when he boarded the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-D|-D}} in [[2368]]. Qol and [[Par Lenor]] came aboard the ''Enterprise''-D after destroying their own [[Par Lenor's shuttle|shuttle]] in a deception designed to convince the ''Enterprise''-D to take them aboard. 

Qol and Lenor were actually interested in the cargo of the ''Enterprise''-D, [[Kamala]], an [[Empathic metamorph]]. Shortly after boarding the vessel, Qol conducted [[Sensor|scans]] of Kamala in [[Cargo bay|cargo bay 4]]. In doing so, he disturbed the safety measures in place and caused the premature emergence of Kamala.

Later, he and Lenor attempted to [[bribe]] [[Ambassador]] [[Briam]] with 20,000 [[coin]]s of [[Ludugial gold]] but they were rejected. When the offended Ambassador said he would inform [[Captain]] [[Jean-Luc Picard|Picard]] of their intentions, the Ferengi attempted to restrain him, a struggle ensued, and Briam was injured, temporarily leaving him in a [[coma]].

Lenor and Qol were transported to [[Starbase 117]] shortly thereafter, where they were expected to face charges.
({{TNG|The Perfect Mate}})
{{bginfo|Qol was played by [[Michael Snyder]].|{{script}}|Like his partner, Qol wore an odd combination of [[Ferengi ranks|rank insignia]] to what was typically established, as [[Ferengi uniform|his uniform]] bore all the hallmarks of a mid-grade officer's uniform, but his [[tattoo]] was that of a [[DaiMon]].}}

{{sidebar individual |image = Nilva.jpg |caption = Nilva |species = [[Ferengi]] |affiliation = [[Ferengi Commerce Authority]] |occupation = [[Commissioner]], [[FCA]]
[[Chairman]] of the [[Slug-o-Cola]] company |spouse = [[Nilva's wife 001|Nilva's wife]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2374 |actor = [[Henry Gibson]] }} '''Nilva''' was a [[Ferengi Commerce Authority]] [[commissioner]] and the [[chairman]] of the [[Slug-o-Cola]] company. Nilva was the only commissioner who agreed to travel to [[Deep Space 9]] in [[2374]] to hear [[Ishka]] talk about the benefits of allowing female [[Ferengi]] to make profit. It was the hope that Nilva would support Ishka's views, which would lead to [[Zek]] being reinstated as [[Grand Nagus]], having been removed from this position for supporting Ishka's feministic ideals and replaced, temporarily, by [[Brunt]]. Before Nilva could arrive, however, Ishka fell ill and was unable to talk with the commissioner. In need of a female to convince Nilva that Ferengi females deserved equal rights as men, Ishka's son, [[Quark]], was surgically altered to resemble a female and assigned to discuss the subject in his mother's place. When Nilva arrived at the [[space station]], he became attracted to Quark, now called "[[Lumba]]". During a dinner, "Lumba" seduced the commissioner, convincing him that equal rights for females could benefit both the Ferengi economy and Nilva's own profits (The main argument of this approach being that clothing includes pockets, and females will thus want to make more money in order to have something to put in those pockets). Later, the two were alone together in Nilva's [[quarters]], as "Lumba" attempted to fend off the commissioner, Brunt burst in and announced that "Lumba" was really a male. "Lumba" then disrobed to reveal "her" body, leaving no doubt that "she" was female. Nilva then left the station, promising to do all he could to see that Zek remained Grand Nagus. ({{DS9|Profit and Lace}}) {{bginfo|Nilva was played by [[Henry Gibson]]. He obviously kept his promise, as Zek was Nagus again when next seen in {{e|The Emperor's New Cloak}}.|Nilva's costume was worn by Francis Scofield for a photoshoot with [[Chris Pine]] for the ''{{el|i254.photobucket.com/albums/hh90/nilvanava/25yvxnn.jpg|December 2009 edition of GQ}}''.}} == External link == * {{mbeta}} [[de:Nilva]] [[ru:Нилва]] [[Category:Ferengi]] [[Category:Ferengi government officials]]

'''Yeggie''' was a [[Ferengi]] who assisted [[Nunk]] in a failed attempt to make a profit by [[kidnapping]] [[Seven of Nine]] to acquire her [[Borg]] [[nanoprobe]]s. 

Their plot was to send a false [[holographic image]] of [[Reginald Barclay]] to steer the {{USS|Voyager}} into a [[geodesic fold]] that would kill the crew. The holographic Barclay was to [[Kidnapping|capture]] Seven to harvest the nanoprobes. Their plot failed when the real Barclay fooled them into closing the fold before ''Voyager'' entered it. ({{VOY|Inside Man}})

{{bginfo|Yeggie was played by [[Christopher Neiman]].|{{script}}}}

{{sidebar individual |image = Kol, 2373.jpg |caption = Kol (2373) |image2 = Kol, 2366.jpg |caption2 = Kol (2366) |species = [[Ferengi]] |affiliation = [[Ferengi Alliance]] |rank = [[File:Ferengi tattoo none graphic.png|25px]] |occupation = [[Pilot]], [[Goss' Marauder]]
[[Lesser Sage]] of the [[Takarian]]s |status = Lost in space |datestatus = 2373 |actor = [[J.R. Quinonez]]
[[Leslie Jordan]] }} {{disambiguation|the Klingon|Kol (Klingon)}} '''Kol''' was a [[male]] [[Ferengi]] [[crewman]] of the [[24th century]] [[Ferengi Alliance]]. In [[2366]], Kol served aboard [[DaiMon]] [[Goss]]' [[Goss' Marauder|marauder]]. When Goss represented the Alliance in the bid for the [[Barzan wormhole]], Kol was one of the [[consul]]s. He and the [[physician]] [[Arridor]] later [[pilot]]ed a [[Arridor's shuttle|shuttle]] into the [[wormhole]], accompanying a [[shuttlepod]] from the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-D|-D}}. Despite warnings that the wormhole had taken the two shuttles to the [[Delta Quadrant]] instead of the [[Gamma Quadrant]] as it was supposed to, the Ferengi refused to follow the [[Starfleet]] shuttle back through the wormhole. Moments after the Starfleet shuttlepod entered the wormhole, its terminus changed, leaving Arridor and Kol stranded in the Delta Quadrant. ({{TNG|The Price}}) Arridor and Kol eventually made their way to the [[Takarian homeworld|homeworld]] of the [[Takarian]]s. They found out about a legend on the planet, told through what was called the [[Song of the Sages]], in which gods were to come to the planet. They passed themselves off as the Holy Sages, he the "[[Lesser Sage]]", and, under this guise, Arridor and Kol obtained vast wealth by demanding tribute from the Takarians over the next seven years. They appointed people to collect dues, such as [[Kafar]], from the various regions and tracked their "earnings" regularly. In [[2373]], the [[planet]] was visited by the {{USS|Voyager}}. Kol was fooled by [[Neelix]], posing first as the [[Grand Proxy]] to the [[Grand Nagus]], and then as the [[Holy Pilgrim]] of the Takarian legend. Unbeknownst to Kol, the last verse of the [[Song of the Sages]] detailed the Sages' departure from the Takarians. Arridor and Kol were captured by ''Voyager'', but soon escaped in their shuttle and attempted to return to {{dis|Takar|region}} but were instead pulled into the Barzan wormhole, making it even more unstable. ({{VOY|False Profits}}) {{bginfo|Kol was portrayed by background actor [[J.R. Quinonez]] in "The Price", and later [[Roles with multiple performers|by]] [[Leslie Jordan]] in "False Profits".|In the script of "False Profits", the character was described thus; "''Kol is not stupid, but he is mean, and has the nervousness and the excitability of a former lackey who has lucked into a windfall of wealth and power – and is ever in fear of losing it.''"}} == External link == * {{mbeta|Kol}} [[de:Kol]] [[fr:Kol (Ferengi)]] [[Category:Ferengi]] [[Category:Ferengi military personnel]] [[Category:Religious leaders]]

'''Nunk''' was a [[male]] [[Ferengi]] who lived during the late [[24th century]], where he commanded a {{class|D'Kora}} [[Nunk's Marauder|Marauder]].

In [[2377]], Nunk saw [[profit]] in obtaining [[Borg]] [[nanoprobe]]s from [[Seven of Nine]], who became known after the {{USS|Voyager}} was contacted by [[Starfleet]]'s [[Pathfinder Project]]. He hired a [[dabo girl]] named [[Leosa]] to seduce [[Lieutenant]] [[Reginald Barclay]] and thereby gain access to information on the Project's transmissions. This included knowledge of {{dis|Reginald Barclay|hologram|a hologram of Barclay}} which was being sent. He positioned his marauder such that it intercepted the program. 

During the next month, he altered the program to convince ''Voyager''{{'}}s crew to execute a plan to get the ship home by creating a fold in space and opening a gateway. Nunk planned to initiate a [[verteron]] pulse in the [[red giant]] star to open a [[geodesic fold]] to bring ''Voyager'' through the fold. This would kill the entire crew, but keep the nanoprobes intact for himself, giving Leosa a cut of the profits. 

Nunk's plan initially succeeded, due to the convincing personality of the hologram, until the final point when they initiated the pulse. The real Barclay pretended to be the hologram and told the Ferengi that Janeway had discovered the plot. He initially wanted to simply leave, but Barclay said they had to close the fold. Nunk did so, which triggered Janeway to stop the process on her end. The hologram tried to [[kidnap]] Seven, but was transported back to the ship. Nunk saw an empty escape pod emerge from the fold and dock with his ship. ({{VOY|Inside Man}})

{{bginfo|Nunk was played by [[Michael William Rivkin]].}}

'''Omag''' was an obese [[Ferengi]] [[arms trader]] during the late-[[24th century]]. He was quite fond of the [[song]] "[[Melor Famagal]]" and [[Qualor II Omag's women 001|beautiful women]].

In [[2368]], he [[stole]] a [[Vulcan]] [[transport]], the ''{{dis|T'Pau|starship}}'', from [[Surplus Depot Z15]] and [[Omag's ship|delivered it]] to a [[Barolian freighter]] at [[Galorndon Core]], near the [[Romulan Neutral Zone]]. [[William T. Riker]] followed him to [[Qualor II]] to seek information about missing [[Vulcan]] ships. Omag was thoroughly disreputable and refused to give any information. Riker threatened to revoke his right of passage in the [[sector]], which would severely hamper his arms dealing. After the threat from Riker, he revealed that the [[Romulan]]s were involved in the theft of Vulcan ships. ({{TNG|Unification II}})

== Appendices ==
=== Background information ===
Omag was played by actor [[William Bastiani]]. He filmed his scenes on Wednesday, {{d|18|September|1991}} on [[Paramount Stage 8]]. 

The script for "Unification II" describes Omag as, "''the fattest Ferengi we've ever seen... on his arms, two gorgeous women in skintight dresses.''" {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/207.txt}}

The combination of his [[Ferengi ranks|rank insignia]] is unique in that [[Ferengi uniform|his uniform]] bore all the hallmarks of a [[DaiMon]]'s uniform, but he did not wear a [[tattoo]] typically associated with DaiMon's, which would become a trend through the remainder of the series. 

In his review of the episode, ''[[Star Trek]]'' author [[Keith R.A. DeCandido]] described Bastiani's performance as "''tiresomely overbearing"''. {{el|tor.com/blogs/2012/06/star-trek-the-next-generation-qunification-iiq}}

=== Apocrypha ===
[[File:Omag -EF2.jpg|thumb|Omag in ''Elite Force II'']]
Omag appears in the {{video game}} ''[[Star Trek: Elite Force II]]'', voiced by [[Matt Malloy]]. In the game, he is a trader working out of a [[Klingon]] [[space station]], who is detained by the crew of the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-E|-E}} for his role in the supply of dangerous weapons of mass destruction. Imprisoned in the brig, Omag eventually reveals whom he sold the weapons to and the location of their control center after the player uses the [[Rules of Acquisition]] to coerce him without violating Federation regulations on the treatment of prisoners.

Omag was also featured in the ''[[Star Trek Customizable Card Game]]''.

'''Morta''' was a [[Ferengi]] [[privateer]] who served under [[DaiMon]] [[Lurin]] in the [[24th century]]. 

In [[2369]], when Lurin attempted to capture and sell a {{class|Galaxy}} [[starship]], Morta, along with [[Berik]] and several other Ferengi, boarded the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-D|-D}} under force. Morta and Berik [[transporter|transported]] onto the [[bridge]] where Morta wounded [[Lieutenant]] [[Worf]] with an [[energy]] [[weapon]]. 

After the capture of the ''Enterprise''-D had been completed, Lurin, threatening to [[execute]] ''Enterprise''-D's civilian personnel, ordered [[Commander]] [[William T. Riker]] to release his lockout of the main computer and instruct Morta on its use. Riker successfully stalled for time by exploiting Morta's dim-wittedness and confusing him with [[technobabble|gibberish]] terms until [[Captain]] [[Jean-Luc Picard|Picard]] could effect a rescue of the bridge. ({{TNG|Rascals}})

{{sidebar individual |image = Goss.jpg |caption = Goss (2366) |species = [[Ferengi]] |affiliation = [[Ferengi Alliance]] |rank = [[File:Ferengi tattoo two graphic.png|25px]] [[File:Ferengi rank pin full.jpg|25px]] [[File:Starfleet captain insignia (2250s-2260s).png|25px]]
[[DaiMon]] |occupation = [[Commanding officer|Commander]], {{Class|D'Kora}} [[Goss' Marauder|marauder]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2366 |actor = [[Scott Thomson]] }} [[DaiMon]] '''Goss''' was a [[24th century]] [[Ferengi]] and the [[CO|commanding officer]] of a {{class|D'Kora}} [[Goss' Marauder|marauder]]. In [[2366]], he demanded the right to negotiate on behalf of the Ferengi for rights to the [[Barzan wormhole]]. Though he had not been invited to the proceedings by the [[Barzan]]s, [[Premier]] [[Bhavani]] agreed to allow their participation. Despite Goss' bluster, however, the Ferengi did not have the resources to compete fairly with the bids of the [[Federation]] or [[Chrysalian]]s. In an effort to gain an edge [[Arridor]] [[distill]]ed [[pyrocyte]]s from Goss' [[blood]] which were used to provoke an extreme [[allergic reaction]] in the Federation's chief [[negotiator]], [[Mendoza]]. When Mendoza fell ill, [[William T. Riker]] was forced to take his place. Riker nearly succeeded in winning the rights to the [[wormhole]] for the Federation but an alliance between Goss and [[Devinoni Ral]], representing the Chrysalians, gave Ral the upper hand. Goss and Ral were so eager to obtain the rights to the wormhole that they did not wait until the results of a mission through the wormhole were analyzed. When Goss' [[consul]]s Arridor and {{dis|Kol|Ferengi}} became trapped in the [[Delta Quadrant]] by the shifting terminus of the wormhole its value as a resource disappeared and Goss was left with no profit to show for his work. ({{TNG|The Price}}) {{bginfo|Goss was played by actor [[Scott Thomson]].|In an either omitted or [[deleted scene]] that appears in the episode's [[script]] was a depiction of the interaction between Ral and Goss that lead to Goss' bluff of destroying the wormhole. In the Scene 65 and 66, immediately following Riker's toast to Ral in Ten Forward, Ral watches as Goss is "at a table trying to pick up a couple of sexy crew women... but as he sits, they exchange a look and leave. Goss is disappointed." Ral joined Goss at the table and explained to the Ferengi that "''Federation women have a game they call "playing hard to get",''" a game which Goss was all too aware of, and which he "[did] not at all find it amusing." Ral then dangles the fact that "''on [[Chrysalia]], the women outnumber the men four to one. They virtually throw themselves at your feet...''" ending the scene with the note, "As Goss' interest perks up considerably..." This scene was immediately followed with Goss' ship leaving orbit and moving to the mouth of the wormhole.}} == External link == * {{mbeta}} [[de:Goss]] [[Category:Ferengi]] [[Category:DaiMons]]

'''Lonzo''' was a [[male]] [[Ferengi]], a known [[tongo]] [[hustler]] on whom [[Odo]] received a [[bulletin]] in [[2371]].

The [[Changeling]], who was at the time "joined" with [[Curzon Dax]] via the ''[[zhian'tara]]'', pointed Lonzo out to [[Jadzia Dax]] and mentioned the bulletin, suggesting they could have fun cleaning the Ferengi out. He then preceded to do exactly that, apologizing to Lonzo as they parted. ({{DS9|Facets}})

{{bginfo|Lonzo was portrayed by background actor [[Mark Barrett]] who received no credit for his role.|His costume was previously worn by [[Lee Arenberg]], portraying the Ferengi {{dis|Gral|Ferengi}} in the episode {{e|The Nagus}} and sold off on the ''[[It's A Wrap! sale and auction]]'' on eBay. {{Sidebar individual |image = Sneed.png |caption = Sneed in 2401 |species = [[Ferengi]] |occupation = [[Crime lord]] |status = [[Deceased]] |datestatus = 2401 |born = [[2342]],
[[Ferenginar]] |died = 2401,
[[M'talas Prime]] |actor = [[Aaron Stanford]] }} {{Aquote|You do realize that 'broker' is just a polite word for 'gangster'? He's a monster!|[[Jae Hwang]]''' to [[Raffaela Musiker]]'''|2401|Disengage}} '''Sneed''' was a [[male]] [[Ferengi]] [[crime lord]] who operated on [[M'talas Prime]] in the early [[25th century]]. He was responsible for creating and distributing the [[narcotic]] {{dis|splinter|drug}}. He collected [[Human]] [[antique]]s, including a {{dis|baseball|object}} and a [[grenade]], and was fond of the [[beverage]] [[Slug-o-Cola]]. Born on [[Ferenginar]] in [[2342]], Sneed grew up as a scavenger in [[District Seven]] of M'talas Prime alongside the [[Vulcan]] [[Krinn]]. The two considered themselves [[brother]]s and had sworn a [[blood oath]] of loyalty to each other. ({{PIC|Disengage|Imposters}}) [[File:Sneed criminal record.png|thumb|left|Sneed's criminal record]] In [[2352]], Sneed was [[arrest]]ed on Ferenginar for falsifying documents and [[fine]]d five bars of [[gold-pressed latinum]] by the [[Ferengi Alliance]]. In [[2364]], the [[Cardassian Union]] arrested him on [[Cardassia]] for [[fraud]], and sentenced him to two years of labor at a [[Bajoran colonies|Bajoran colony]]. In [[2370]], he was caught [[smuggling]] in [[Federation space]] and imprisoned for four years. In [[2384]], he was again arrested by the [[Federation]] for committing [[arson]] on [[Deep Space 9]], and imprisoned for three months. Sneed's known associates included [[Jae Hwang]] of [[Earth]], [[Larell]] of [[Renhia]], [[Morn]] of [[Luria]], [[Quark]] of [[Ferenginar]], [[Brunt]] of Ferenginar, and [[Thadiun Okona]] of the [[Omega Sagitta system]]. In [[2401]], Sneed was paid by rogue [[Changeling]] [[Titus Rikka]] to orchestrate the destruction of a [[Starfleet]] recruitment center, using a [[portal weapon]] the Changelings had stolen from [[Daystrom Station]]. He framed [[Romulan]] rebel [[Lurak T'Luco]] for the attack, which prompted [[Commander]] [[Raffi Musiker]], via her ex-husband Jae, to arrange a meeting with Sneed at his lair in [[District Six]]. During the meeting, Musiker claimed to work for T'Luco, which Sneed knew to be false as he had already had T'Luco [[murder]]ed to cover his tracks and was keeping his severed [[head]] with him as a [[trophy]]. Sneed coerced Musiker into taking splinter to try and expose her true employer. When this failed, he ordered his [[bodyguard]]s to kill her, but she managed to escape with the timely appearance of [[Worf]], who [[behead]]ed Sneed during the ensuing melee. ({{PIC|Disengage|Seventeen Seconds}}) [[File:Picard and Riker access files.jpg|thumb|Sneed's record, among Ro's files]] Sneed's death left a power vacuum in the District Six underworld, which Worf and Musiker exploited to draw out his "brother" Krinn, so as to learn how the Changelings' breach of Daystrom Station had been accomplished. His file was among the data collected by [[Commander]] [[Ro Laren]] pertaining to the Changeling infiltration of Starfleet, which she passed to [[Admiral]] [[Jean-Luc Picard]] shortly before her death. ({{PIC|Imposters}}) {{bginfo|Sneed was played by [[Aaron Stanford]].|[[Armin Shimerman]], who played [[Quark]], admired Stanford's performance, recalling in an interview, "''I turned to my [[Kitty Swink|wife]] and said, 'That's the way I should have played the Ferengi from the first'... [Sneed] was both cunning and oily and believable and less cartoonish... it would have been an entirely different species if I had played a Ferengi as well as that actor played it.''" ''{{el|indiewire.com/features/general/star-trek-deep-space-nine-picard-tv-show-1234829883/}}''}} [[Category:Ferengi]]
